# Incident Report: 2021-09-10 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.9.10.102** |
| MAC address | **00:4f:49:b1:e8:c3** (confirmed via ARP: `10.9.10.102 <-> 00:4f:49:b1:e8:c3`, matches DHCP lease) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-KKITB6Q** (NBNS `<00>`/`<20>` records, DHCP option 12, LDAP `CN=DESKTOP-KKITB6Q,CN=Computers,DC=angrypoutine,DC=com`) |
| Logged-in domain user | **hobart.gunnarsson** (Kerberos `CNameString`, AS-REQ/TGS traffic between 10.9.10.102 and DC 10.9.10.9) |
| Windows domain | angrypoutine.com (DC: ANGRYPOUTINE-DC / 10.9.10.9) |

## Malware Family and Attribution
**Attribution: behavioral** (no Suricata/IDS alert files were provided alongside the pcap, so nothing here is signature-confirmed).

The infection chain matches the **Hancitor** downloader/gate pattern, followed by a **Cobalt Strike** beacon as the final payload:

1. At T+140s the victim issued an HTTP GET to `simpsonsavingss.com` (194.62.42.206) for `/bmdff/BhoHsCtZ/MLdmpfjaX/5uFG3Dz7yt/date1?BNLv65=pAAS`, using the spoofed legacy user-agent `Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; WOW64; Trident/7.0; ...)` — a hallmark of Hancitor gate check-ins (random-looking multi-segment URI path, `date`-prefixed endpoint name, fake old-IE UA on a modern OS).
2. The server responded `200 OK`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="date6"`, delivering a **284,816-byte PE32+ DLL** (Windows NT 10.0 x64) — exported and hashed from the capture (see IOCs).
3. Shortly after (T+144s onward), the host began making TLS connections to two unrelated external IPs on port 443 with **no SNI extension** and presenting **the same self-signed certificate** (Subject/Issuer `CN=londonarealoeli.uk, OU=UK System, O=LL EST, L=London, ST=London, C=UK`, serial differs per host). Identical templated self-signed certs served from two separate VPS IPs with blank SNI is a well-known Cobalt Strike C2 default-cert pattern.
4. One of the two C2 hosts (94.158.245.52) shows irregular repeat check-ins over ~75 minutes (T+148s through T+4512s), consistent with beacon behavior rather than user-driven browsing.
5. At T+254s the host also queried `myexternalip.com` over TLS (34.117.59.81) — a common post-compromise recon step to fingerprint the victim's public IP, consistent with a loader/beacon staging itself.

Everything else in the capture (Windows Update/Delivery Optimization `.cab`/`.exe` downloads, Microsoft telemetry, `msftncsi`, Office/Teams/OneDrive/Bing/Store traffic, SSDP/mDNS/LLMNR/NBNS/Kerberos/LDAP/SMB domain traffic) is normal enterprise Windows background noise and is listed as benign context, not IOCs.

## Indicators of Compromise

| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C2 endpoint | **167.172.37.9:443** | TLS handshake, no SNI, self-signed cert CN=londonarealoeli.uk, serial `6e77ccef...` |
| C2 endpoint | **94.158.245.52:443** | TLS handshake, no SNI, same self-signed cert template (CN=londonarealoeli.uk), serial `0fa40f28...`; repeat beacon connections over ~75 min |
| Malicious domain | **simpsonsavingss.com** | HTTP Host header, resolved to 194.62.42.206, served the DLL payload |
| Malicious URL | `http://simpsonsavingss.com/bmdff/BhoHsCtZ/MLdmpfjaX/5uFG3Dz7yt/date1?BNLv65=pAAS` | Full GET request/response captured in TCP stream, tshark follow output |
| Transferred file | **date6** (server `Content-Disposition` filename; delivered from URI `.../date1`) | HTTP response headers, `Content-Length: 284816`, `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` |
| File hash (SHA256) | **eed363fc4af7a9070d69340592dcab7c78db4f90710357de29e3b624aa957cf8** | Computed directly from the exported HTTP object (PE32+ DLL, 284,816 bytes) |

## Benign Context (not indicators)
- `simpsonsavingss.com` HTTP transaction's own destination IP conversation partner set (`23.1.237.225`, `23.1.237.216`, `23.1.237.200`, `23.1.237.201`, `52.238.248.6`, `23.3.x.x`, `104.x.x.x`, `13.107.x.x`, `20.x.x.x`, `52.109.x.x`, `40.x.x.x`, `72.21.81.200`) — all Windows Update, Delivery Optimization, Microsoft Store, Office 365, Bing, MSN, OneDrive, Teams, login.live.com, and telemetry endpoints (confirmed by TLS SNI / HTTP Host).
- `myexternalip.com` (34.117.59.81) — legitimate public service, only its use here is noted as a TTP, not itself malicious.
- Internal domain traffic: `angrypoutine.com`, DC `ANGRYPOUTINE-DC` (10.9.10.9), Kerberos/LDAP/SMB/NBNS/DHCP among 10.9.10.102, 10.9.10.103, 10.9.10.9, 10.9.10.1.

## Incident Summary
The Windows 10 workstation **DESKTOP-KKITB6Q** (10.9.10.102, MAC 00:4f:49:b1:e8:c3), logged in as domain user **hobart.gunnarsson** on the angrypoutine.com domain, was infected via a **Hancitor-style gate** at `simpsonsavingss.com` that delivered a 284,816-byte 64-bit DLL payload (SHA256 `eed363fc4af7a9070d69340592dcab7c78db4f90710357de29e3b624aa957cf8`) using a spoofed legacy Internet Explorer user-agent. Within seconds the host began beaconing over TLS (no SNI, shared self-signed "londonarealoeli.uk" certificate) to two external IPs, 167.172.37.9:443 and 94.158.245.52:443, consistent with a **Cobalt Strike** post-exploitation C2 channel, with the second host showing sustained beacon activity for over an hour. Attribution to Hancitor/Cobalt Strike is behavioral, based on URI/UA/delivery-chain and certificate-reuse patterns; no IDS/Suricata alerts were provided to confirm by signature.
